builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted model uses more compute or memory than your workload can justify.
builder_plan.change: Check for a usable pruned checkpoint and runtime support before attempting model surgery.
builder_plan.baseline: The original unpruned model at the same precision, context, and load.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task quality, actual GPU memory, serving throughput, and preparation cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Complete-SVD: A Functional Norm Approach to Low-Rank LLM Compression
summary: Complete-SVD replaces plain truncated SVD and prior output-aware weighting schemes for post-training low-rank LLM compression by minimizing a linearized, Kronecker-factored L2 logit-distance objective with a closed-form weighted-SVD solution, whose output-side factor is estimated unbiasedly from random probes. Its cost is K backward passes per calibration sequence (vocabulary- and length-independent) plus calibration data, and the compressed model still carries the quality loss inherent to the chosen rank ratio, with no measured inference speedup reported. It can fail when the linearization around original weights is inaccurate at aggressive compression, when the probe estimate is noisy at small K, or when calibration is unrepresentative, as the KL-SVD variant shows by improving calibration perplexity while degrading cross-corpus perplexity.
rationale: Post-training low-rank compression with a closed-form solver and probe-based estimation fits a single 24 GB GPU and no retraining, but the reported gains are perplexity and accuracy comparisons rather than a measured multiplicative speedup, so the reader must validate the quality-versus-compression tradeoff on their own model and workload before adopting.

claims.statement: Complete-SVD replaces plain truncated SVD and prior output-aware weighting schemes for post-training low-rank LLM compression by minimizing a linearized, Kronecker-factored L2 logit-distance objective with a closed-form weighted-SVD solution, whose output-side factor is estimated unbiasedly from random probes. Its cost is K backward passes per calibration sequence (vocabulary- and length-independent) plus calibration data, and the compressed model still carries the quality loss inherent to the chosen rank ratio, with no measured inference speedup reported. It can fail when the linearization around original weights is inaccurate at aggressive compression, when the probe estimate is noisy at small K, or when calibration is unrepresentative, as the KL-SVD variant shows by improving calibration perplexity while degrading cross-corpus perplexity.

At matched settings with uniform ranks and WikiText-2 calibration, Complete-SVD achieves the lowest C4 and PTB perplexity in every setting, and at ratio 0.7 under LEMS rank allocation; KL-SVD lowers calibration perplexity and raises downstream accuracy; Complete-SVD improves IFEval instruction-following accuracy over the strongest prior output-aware methods.
